# Utilities whose corpus does not yet pass on Darwin.
#
# The macOS lane runs the WHOLE catalogue and compares the set of test
# functions that failed against this list. A name that fails and is not here
# fails the lane — that is the ratchet, and it is what stops the Darwin
# result from drifting while the divergences are worked through.
#
# Entries only ever LEAVE. When a utility's Darwin branch lands, its line is
# deleted in the same change, and the lane starts holding it to GNU from then
# on. Nothing is ever added to buy a green lane: a new name here means a
# utility that used to pass on Darwin now does not, which is a regression to
# fix rather than to record.
#
# Thirteen more left when the fixture work was finished properly. The first
# pass converted the sites matching one spelling; there were four more, and a
# harness that never consulted the skip flag at all. What was left after that
# was not GNU divergence either: a Linux-only path the harness opens, a unix
# socket address longer than Darwin's 104-byte limit, a cross-device case with
# no second filesystem to reach, and `stat -f %c` — the filesystem's live inode
# total, which the corpus listed as stable because ext4 fixes it at mkfs time
# and APFS does not.
#
# TestMulticallParity was briefly listed here and should not have been. It
# compares the standalone binary against the multicall one and never consults
# GNU, so it does not belong in a ledger of GNU divergences; it was failing on
# the fixtures above, and it passes now.
#
# Eight names left in one change: their only Darwin failure was a fixture —
# the corpus builds a file whose NAME is not valid UTF-8, APFS refuses it with
# EILSEQ, and the t.Fatal fired while the corpus was being BUILT, taking the
# utility's whole parity test down before a case ran. Those cases skip on such
# a filesystem now and the rest are held to GNU, which also put 3186
# comparisons back that had never run.
#
# One test function per line, so the granularity is a utility rather than a
# case. The case counts behind these names, and the clusters they fall into,
# are in #9714; the largest by far is the listing code behind vdir, ls and
# dir, which is one program and 43% of the failures.

# min-tests: 19000
#
# A run that executed fewer tests than this is not a measurement, and the
# gate refuses it rather than believing its narrower failure set. This file
# is the reason that check exists.
#
# The first 51 entries came from a run described as complete which was not:
# it executed 14814 of 19913 tests. `numfmt --padding=99999999999999999999`
# is a valid invocation that GNU answers with about 10^20 spaces, and the
# harness captured it unbounded — 95 GB and climbing at 400 MB/s, with
# enough memory pressure to get tests running beside it killed. So the run
# died away in the tail, every file from pwd_test.go onward went unmeasured,
# and 32 utilities were recorded as PASSING without ever having run. 5a6dcb7
# capped the capture; the first round after it completed, and those 32
# surfaced at once and read as regressions (#9721 and #9740 both hit that).
#
# They are pre-existing divergences, and the proof is in the source rather
# than in a log: utmpx is unimplemented, so who, users and uptime print
# nothing at all, and the non-UTF-8 filename fixtures cannot be created on
# APFS. #9714 owns all of it.
#
# The errno WORDING was a third such cause and is now fixed: both copies of
# the strerror text — internal/strerror for the runtime's IoError.Other, and
# coreutils/lib/gnu.fern for the errnos a utility names itself — carry the
# Darwin libc's words on a Darwin build. Whichever of the names below were
# failing on that alone now pass, and the lane reports a listed utility that
# passes as a warning; each one it names leaves this file.
#
# Re-seeded from two independent complete runs that agreed on this set
# byte-for-byte: 35356807225 and 35372825718, 1887 failures over 19913 tests.
